name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: The Origin Story of India's States
description:
**About the Lecture**

15 August 1947. It is tempting to think of this as the singular date on which India was formed. But India did not come into being all at once. The process of its formation continued long after Independence, as regions were reorganised, boundaries redrawn, and new states created.

The stories of India’s states are, in many ways, the story of India itself.

States are more than administrative boundaries on a map. They are places where we grow up, build friendships, find work, and make memories. They shape our languages, cultures, identities and our sense of home. Every time a state is created or an existing one is altered, the country and its people are reshaped in the process.

In this lecture, we’ll go beyond memorising capitals and marking boundaries on a school atlas. Through stories, historical details and a quiz to get us thinking, we’ll explore the events, ideas and movements that shaped the states we know today.

Why was a particular state created? What did its borders look like before? How did language, politics, culture and history influence its formation? And what do these stories tell us about the country we call home?

Whether you grew up in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bengal, or somewhere else entirely, there’s a story here that belongs to you.

After all, every Indian deserves to know the origin story of their state.

**About the Lecturer**

Venkataraghavan Srinivasan is a writer and actor whose work spans multiple mediums and genres.

In nonfiction, he wrote The Origin Story of India’s States and his forthcoming book, Lights! Camera! Democracy! The Cinematic Politics of Tamil Nadu.

He is also the author of the children’s book Brachio and was the first recipient of the Neev Fellowship for Children’s Book Creators. His short fiction has appeared in The Iowa Review and The Bombay Literary Magazine, among other publications, and has been included in anthologies and prize shortlists.

Alongside his writing, he works as a performer on stage and screen. Before pursuing these creative interests, he worked in brand strategy in advertising. He grew up in Bangalore and now lives in Chennai.

At Pint of View, he brings his work on the history of India’s states to the barroom classroom, helping us look at familiar places with a fresh perspective.

**About Pint of View**

Pint of View is India's Largest Lecture Community. We brought the lecture in bar format to India and are now expanding across the globe with chapters in 16 cities worldwide. Here, big ideas meet intimate spaces, and you walk in curious and walk out with a sharper lens on the world.

Book now and develop your own pint of view. 🍻

An ode to Bollywood's darker side.

Halloween has a different kind of horror when Bollywood gets involved.

Forget the usual Halloween playbook. This year, The Shift pays homage to Bollywood and the horror films that gave us haunted havelis, sinister secrets, supernatural encounters, unforgettable villains, and stories that stayed with us long after the credits rolled.

On October 30, we're bringing that universe to life with a night that blends cinematic nostalgia, unapologetic music, and a little beautiful madness. This isn't Halloween as you know it. This is Helloween, the Bollywood way.

**BEHIND THE DECKS**

**DJ Jasmeet** — Known for high-energy sets and an instinct for reading the dance floor, DJ Jasmeet brings Bollywood favourites into the world of electronic and club sounds. Expect familiar hooks, unexpected switches, and a dance floor that doesn't stay still for long.

**Sa-Rang** — Bringing together Bollywood, Bollytech, and Amapiano, Sa-Rang adds another dimension to the night's sound. Expect the nostalgia of Bollywood meeting electronic rhythms and global dance-floor energy.

**Bombay Daak** — A modern take on India's culture, Bombay Daak celebrates the spirit of neighborhood drinking spots through inventive cocktails, nostalgic influences, and food made to be enjoyed over another round. Expect a bar takeover with character, where what's in the glass is just as much a part of the experience as what's happening around you.

**IMPORTANT:** A Helloween costume is mandatory. No costume, no entry. No refunds will be issued.

You’re invited to an exclusive preview of BuCo., a first taste of our menu before we officially open our doors in Bangalore.

BuCo. began in Mangaluru, a coastal town whose flavours have always deserved more attention than they get. We started as an artisanal bakery built on one belief: the best food comes from knowing exactly where your ingredients come from and exactly what you’re doing with them.

Today, BuCo. is a modern neighbourhood cafe rooted in Karnataka’s culture.

Our menu is anchored in regional flavours and seasonal produce, with a fully in-house bakery that brings European baking techniques to local ingredients. All of it is backed by a serious filter coffee program.

Everything is made in house, and every element is locally sourced. We don’t take shortcuts. That isn’t because it’s trendy. It’s because the food demands it.

After our flagship store in the heart of Mangaluru, we’re now bringing BuCo. to Bangalore.

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: Murder in the Expanding Universe—Investigating Dark Energy & the Possible Death of the Cosmological Constant
description:
**About the event**

Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

The Universe is expanding, and one quantity, the cosmological constant, has been known to explain why the expansion is speeding up.... until now.

New data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) hints that the cosmological constant may not be constant after all.

Inspired by the film noir genre, this talk will address what we know about the Universe’s expansion so far, and whether the cosmological constant is dead for good. We will visit the crime scene, flash back through a century of clues, and question the witnesses: galaxies and quasars that each saw the universe at a different moment in time.

We will line up the suspects who may or may not have killed the cosmological constant, and cross-examine them with evidence that the Universe naturally provides us.

Here’s a case that is far from being open-and-shut.

**About the Speaker**

Dr. Basundhara Ghosh is a faculty of Physics at Azim Premji University, Bengaluru, and specialises in Theoretical Cosmology.

Prior to this, she was a DST-INSPIRE Faculty and a CV Raman Postdoctoral Fellow at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, and a DAAD Research Fellow at Heidelberg University, Germany.

She obtained her PhD from the University of Geneva, Switzerland and her MSc from the Indian Institute of Technology Bhubaneswar. Her research interests encompass the study of the Universe at late times, also known as the dark energy- dominated epoch.

When she is not studying the Universe or teaching in a classroom, she discusses films on her Instagram page @gangsofcinepur.

name: Signal Traces: Bengaluru by Thomas Lea Clarke
description:
Join us for the final presentation of Thomas Lea Clarke, bangaloREsident@Indian Music Experience Museum, before he heads back to Germany.

*Signal Traces: Bengaluru* is an exhibition by artist Thomas Lea Clarke, developed over two months spent listening to Bengaluru and discussing sound, music and memory with people whose lives and work engage with sound in different ways. Through interviews with musicians, artists, technicians, residents, instrument builders, a sound archaeologist and a neuroscientist, Clarke explores how sound lives on in recordings, voices, bodies, spaces and objects, and how different forms of listening can affect the experience of our environments.

The exhibition takes the form of a four-channel sound installation, a photographic series and a publication. In the sound installation, fragments of recorded conversations move through the space alongside field recordings and musical elements, forming a shifting listening environment in which personal recollection, everyday sound, musical practice and the material cultures of listening intersect. The photographic series focuses on the people, objects and spaces encountered during the project, tracing the physical environments and material forms through which sound is made, stored, repaired, transmitted and remembered. The publication presents the interviews in longer form, allowing conversations heard only fragmentarily within the installation to retain their individual context and complexity.

**Saturday, October 31**

**6:30pm onwards**

**Indian Music Experience Museum**

name: The C+C Diwali Party
description:
*Diwali is always a little more special when it's shared with good people, good food, and traditions that take you back home.*

Whether you've grown up celebrating Diwali, are looking to reconnect with familiar traditions, or are spending the festive season away from home, we'd love to have you join us at **The C+C Diwali Party**! We're bringing together everything we love about Diwali: **a delicious, nourishing spread of festive treats, the nostalgic games** we grew up playing, and the little traditions that make this time of year feel so special. There'll be an **art corner** where you can paint your own **diya, mehendi cones** to get into the festive spirit, and plenty of opportunities to eat, play, and get to know the people around you.

If you're new to Bangalore, away from family, or simply want to join the festive cheer and find your community here, consider this your invitation. Bring your friends, come along with family, or show up on your own. There's always room for one more at our table!

And of course, we **highly recommend coming dressed in your best Diwali fits!**

*Let's make some new memories, revisit a few old ones, and celebrate Diwali together, the way it should be: surrounded by good food, good company, and a community that makes you feel at home.*

name: The Humming Tree x Indian Music Experience x Jodhpur RIFF present Killabeatmaker (Colombia)
description:
**About the Artist:**

KillaBeatmaker is a Medellín-based Colombian DJ, producer, singer-songwriter and audio engineer known for blending ancestral South American and Afro-Colombian sounds with electronic bass and global club rhythms. His live band expands this sound into a dynamic fusion of live percussion, Colombian flute, synthesizers, vocals and electronic production, bringing together traditional instrumentation and contemporary club music.

Joined by Guadalupe and Yulian, the live setup combines Colombian folk percussion and gaita with Akai-driven sequences, MPCs and synths, creating an immersive, rhythm-heavy performance rooted in Colombia while looking firmly toward the global dance floor.

**The Humming Tree:**

The Humming Tree - A grassroots performance venue in Bangalore, running from 2013 to 2019 and in the process becoming a cornerstone of Bangalore’s independent music, art, and cultural ecosystem.

Now, in 2026, The Humming Tree is back in a brand-new, purpose-designed space in Indiranagar. Built across 12,000 sq. ft., the venue features a 600+ capacity performance space, world-class sound and lighting systems, and a diverse F&B proposition. More than just a venue, it’s a hub for creativity, culture and collaboration.

name: An Hour of Stillness - An immersive sound experience
description:
Somewhere between the demands of the day and the things waiting for tomorrow, there is a little space to pause.

Join Sri for an immersive 60-minute sound experience with Himalayan singing bowls, crystal bowls, handpan, ocean drum and gong.

Through layers of sound, moments of quiet and a gentle return to the present, you'll have an hour to simply listen.

There's nothing to learn, no experience required and nothing you need to achieve.

Just come as you are. Get comfortable. Listen.

**What to expect**

- A gentle arrival and grounding
- An immersive journey through live instrumental sounds
- Moments of quiet and stillness
- Time to return slowly before the session closes

**Who is this for?**

Anyone looking to step away from the demands of everyday life and make a little room for themselves. No prior meditation or sound experience is needed.
